title: Deep learning maps fine-scale plant distributions and fire-associated change
summary: DeepBiosphere combines a residual CNN trained on citizen-science observations with aerial imagery to map California distributions for 2,221 plant species. The authors report median AUC 0.95 versus 0.88 for climate-only models and use repeat imagery to map plant-community change associated with the 2013 Rim Fire. These are California-specific ecological maps and observational associations; the study does not establish causal effects of fire or a new species discovery.
ai_technology: DeepBiosphere residual convolutional neural network for species-distribution mapping

evidence.tested: The primary article reports held-out mapping median AUC 0.95 versus 0.88 for climate-only models and uses repeat imagery to map community change following the 2013 Rim Fire.
evidence.unknown: The fire-severity relationship is observational and does not establish causation. Mapping performance is California-specific and weaker for rare species.
evidence.ai_role: A residual CNN trained with citizen-science observations and aerial imagery produced fine-scale species-distribution maps that were then used to estimate rapid plant-community change.

source_review.scope: Primary PNAS indexed article and PMC full-text indexed content, including abstract, Methods, results and plant/fire case studies; PubMed primary metadata/affiliations and first-online date.
